To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Chicxub impact was not the cause of the Cretaceous–Tertiary boundary hiatus in North Atlantic deep-sea sediment sections, but rather a result of tectonic activity associated with increased volcanism in the Caribbean and Iberian Peninsula.
the KTB in the North Atlantic was marked by a major hiatus and mass wasting, but not by the Chicxulup impact.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Chicxub impact is not the ultimate cause of the KTB mass extinction.
the Chicxubul impact did not cause the KTB mass extinction, but that the impact was a major event of the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary transition.
the Chicxubul impact did not cause mass wasting and hiatuses in the North Atlantic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Chicxubil impact was not responsible for the mass wasting and hiatuses in the North Atlantic.
mass wasting was the result of earthquakes, not the Chicxulup impact.
the KTB is not the best time interval for studying the mass extinction and that the Chicxub impact is not the best candidate for causing the mass extinction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the KTB is not always associated with mass wasting and hiatuses, and that the latter can occur in the early Danians well after the KTB, as observed at other sites in the North Atlantic and the Caribbean.
mass wasting and hiatuses are not unique to the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary and can be the result of a variety of processes unrelated to the KTB.
the Chicxubul impact is not the cause of the KTB mass wasting in the North Atlantic, but that the Chicxubl impact and the mass wasting events in the North Atlantic were separated by ~ 100 ky.
